newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Volume picks up, mostly on calls.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Volume picks up, mostly on calls.

text.p: Several individual equity options had heavy volume Thursday, most of it on the call side, suggesting to some options analysts that the broader U.S. stock market may be ready for a decline.
In an afternoon report, Jerry Hegarty, an analyst at Thomson Financial Services, noted that the equity put/call ratio was 0.47, meaning about twice as many equity calls traded as puts.
"The market will eventually feel the pressure of this optimism and sell off," he said, adding that Thursday's reading would be the fourth bearish reading in five sessions.
Contrarians view heavy call buying as a sign of excessive optimism that would suggest a selloff.
But much of Thursday's call activity was centered on a few issues such as General Electric Co, Telebras, Office Depot Inc and Nike Inc.
The Telebras January 125 call traded 13,668 contracts on the American Stock Exchange, which compares with open interest of 18,946.
With Telebras shares in the U.S. down two at 135-1/4 Thursday afternoon, the option lost 3/8 to 22-3/4.
Close behind was the Office Depot July 15 call, which traded roughly 13,000 contracts.
That option, which was up 1/8 at 3-3/4, had open interest of 51,643. The stock was up 1/4 at 17-1/4.
Office Depot July options have been fairly active recently as investors await a U.S. District Court ruling on its planned merger with Staples Inc. The ruling is expected in mid-June.
In General Electric options, the June 40 call traded 10,235 contracts and the January 1998 40 call traded around 10,000 in what traders said was basically a roll.
"It was a close on the Junes and an open on the January side," said a market maker. "It gave us a busy morning."
Michael Schwartz, a managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, said the move could have been done as a tax-deferral strategy.

"The motivation could be for taxes to defer the gain until January 1998 with some assurance that as long as it stays above 40, it's going to be exercised," he said. "It looks like a tax-deferral technique more than anything else to me."
Elsewhere, Nike options were fairly busy as the stock fell sharply after the company warned its fiscal fourth quarter earnings would fall short of analysts' expectations.
A market maker on the Pacific Exchange, where Nike options trade, said activity was "orderly busy" with much of the volume coming from investors closing positions.
"It's actively trading on the (stock) move," he said. "Volatility's up a litle bit but it looks like things are settling down." Nike shares dropped nine to 55.
The most active Nike options were the June 60 put and June 55 call, which traded 4,850 and 4,335 options, respectively.
The market maker also noted that there was a "very active' buyer in a couple of WorldCom Inc calls, namely the January 25 calls and the September 27-1/2 calls.
